description.narrative:
The First Climate Council of Türkiye, held in the City of Konya in 2022, represented a crucial milestone in addressing the pressing challenges posed by climate change in the country. With a commitment to aligning national climate policies with the global objectives of the Paris Agreement, the council provided a platform for policymakers, experts, and stakeholders to come together and deliberate on effective strategies for climate action.
Throughout the council's proceedings, a series of panels engaged in comprehensive discussions, culminating in a set of decisions and policy recommendations that would guide Türkiye's future actions to combat climate change. Among these recommendations, a notable section focused on Just Transition, underscoring the significance of ensuring a fair and equitable shift towards a low-carbon and sustainable economy. This emphasis on Just Transition reflects Türkiye's commitment to safeguarding the interests of workers and communities affected by the transition to green and sustainable practices.
The Ministry of Labour and Social Security prepared and adopted the “Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights” in November 2022 in consultation with the social partners, Ministry of Justice and the ILO. The ILO contribution to the Climate Council consistently highlighted the importance of incorporating Just Transition principles, promoting green jobs, and fostering meaningful social dialogue. The ILO's expertise proved instrumental in guiding the council's considerations towards socially inclusive and environmentally responsible solutions.
As a result of the collaborative efforts and the principled advocacy championed by the ILO during the panel meetings, the final decisions of the Climate Council prominently reflected the concerns surrounding Just Transition, green job creation, and social dialogue. The inclusion of these elements in the council's recommendations signifies a commitment to adopting climate policies that prioritize both environmental sustainability and social justice.
As a joint initiative, ILO and UNDP published a report titled « Social and Employment Impacts of Climate Change and Green Economy Policies in Türkiye », which served as a tool for ILO to advocate for adaption of a job-rich green agenda by the government.
The Ministry of Labour and Social Security prepared and adopted the “Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights”. The Guiding Principles are in line with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and is prepared in accordance with the National Action Plan on Human Rights. The Guiding Principles covers all areas of Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work and directly refers to relevant ILO Conventions. The ILO supported the process by providing technical support.

description.narrative:
The SCORE program was successfully implemented in the supplier enterprises of international apparel brands like H&M and INDITEX. The suppliers and the brands integrated the SCORE program into their annual implementation plans on sustainability and compliance, which is showcase of the willingness of the companies to further enhancing the positive impact on the working conditions and productivity of the participating SMEs.
The Entrepreneurship Support Programme, which was designed with ILO’s technical support, aimed at fostering economic empowerment and self-reliance amongst refugee and host community entrepreneurs was implemented in collaboration with techno-parks under universities in Mersin, Sanliurfa and Konya.The Programme provided training, seminars and one-to-one mentorships to 257 entrepreneurs as well as grants up to 100.000TRY for 98 beneficiary enterprises.
Moreover, under the scope of social solidarity economy support programme, financial and technical capacities of 4 women cooperatives in Türkiye, in which both refugee and host community women are the members of, have been improved in collaboration with the Ministry of Labour and Social Security.
The ILO’s implementation of the “Gender Equality at Enterprises Model” at KARSAN company, an affiliate of employers’ organization MESS/TISK, resulted in improved working conditions and a remarkable increase in the number of women employees at the company. ILO provided technical support to the delivery of SCORE program with the financial support of EU Regional Trust Fund in Response to the Syria Crisis (MADAD-FRIT). The productivity and working conditions at the SMEs are enhanced. ILO has put remarkable efforts to establish "enterprise improvement teams" within these SMEs, a novel application that enterprise managements had not tried before. Within the reporting period,106 workers employed under 8 enterprises have benefitted from programme, which reached out to 509 workers and 60 enterprises in total (between 2018-2022).
In collaboration with technoparks, ILO has designed and implemented the activities under the Entrepreneurship Support Programme, which was co-funded by MADAD-FRIT and United States Department of State, Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration (USDOS PRM). The ILO provided various services beyond financial aid. These include identification, selection, formalization, complementary business development support, information sharing, communication of the results and advocacy. ILO also played a role in strengthening collaborations with local stakeholders and municipalities, creating a supportive environment for enterprise formalization.
ILO provided necessary financial and technical contribution to promote the sustainability of the refugee and host community women run cooperatives, in collaboration with Ministry of Labour and Social Services (MoLSS), through PRM funds. Supports include delivery of SWOT/TOWS analysis, machinery and financial supports, trainings on various topics including, but not limited to vocational skills, relevant regulations & rights of cooperative members.
ILO followed up on the implementation of Swedish funded “Gender Equality at Enterprises Model”, in KARSAN company. The company recruited 160 female blue-collar employees for the first time, as a result of the improved working conditions.
